One action set to `all` reaches the whole account's live reads that spend no budget of their own (notifications, profile analytics, SSI, profile visitors, the invitation and saved-list listings): those calls debit no action type, so they have none to read this setting from and take the account-wide answer instead. Reads that DO debit an action type read that action type's own setting.

warm_up_state.description: READ-ONLY. The warm-up ramp state active on this row: the label for `warm_up_factor` beside it, derived from it, so the two always agree. A value sent here is still checked for being a state at all, and is then accepted and ignored: it is never stored and never recorded in the ledger. Set `warm_up_factor` to pin a row out of the ramp Curviate derives for the account.

warm_up_factor.description: Multiplier applied to this row's ceiling while ramping. 1 is not ramping.

character_cap.description: Length cap on this row's free-text field, in characters (an invitation note, an InMail body).

subject_character_cap.description: Length cap on this row's subject line, in characters.

per_query_cap.description: Bound on a single query's result lines. Search rows only.

source_class.description: How well calibrated this row's configured number is. Overriding it labels your own figure; the over-default warning always reports the class of the Curviate default.

effective_ceiling.description: READ-ONLY. `ceiling` with the account's warm-up ramp applied, which is what this row is actually held to. Sent back on a write it is accepted and ignored, so the whole document round-trips; it is never stored and never ledgered.

interface_ceiling.description: READ-ONLY. What a call through the matching elevated interface (`/v1/{account_id}/sales-navigator/...`, `/v1/{account_id}/recruiter/...`) is held to on this row, or null when this row and limit profile have no such figure. `ceiling`, `effective_ceiling`, `band` and `over_default` are all the STANDARD-interface figure, so on a `sales_navigator` or `recruiter` account a row can report `over` while a call through the elevated interface still succeeds. Sent back on a write it is accepted and ignored, so the whole document round-trips; it is never stored and never ledgered.

effective_interface_ceiling.description: READ-ONLY. `interface_ceiling` with the account's warm-up ramp applied. Read THIS to know where an elevated-interface call stops, for the same reason `effective_ceiling` and not `ceiling` answers that for a standard one. Sent back on a write it is accepted and ignored, so the whole document round-trips; it is never stored and never ledgered.

posture_source.description: READ-ONLY. Which scope supplied this row's effective `posture`. Sent back on a write it is accepted and ignored, so the whole document round-trips; it is never stored and never ledgered.

over_default.description: READ-ONLY. The fields on this row configured above the Curviate default. Sent back on a write it is accepted and ignored, so the whole document round-trips; it is never stored and never ledgered.

rows.description: Per-row configuration. Each entry names its `budget_row` and the fields to change. A row read back from the policy document may be sent here unchanged: its read-only fields (`effective_ceiling`, `posture_source`, `over_default`, `warm_up_state`) are accepted and ignored.

object.description: READ-ONLY. The document's type discriminator. Sent back on a write it is accepted and ignored, so the whole document round-trips; it is never stored and never ledgered.

account_id.description: READ-ONLY. The account this document describes; the path names it. Sent back on a write it is accepted and ignored, so the whole document round-trips; it is never stored and never ledgered.

seat_tier_mismatch.description: READ-ONLY. The Curviate seat tier that disagrees with `limit_profile`. Sent back on a write it is accepted and ignored, so the whole document round-trips; it is never stored and never ledgered.

posture_source.description: READ-ONLY. Which scope supplied this account's effective `posture`. Sent back on a write it is accepted and ignored, so the whole document round-trips; it is never stored and never ledgered.

warm_up.description: READ-ONLY. The account's DERIVED warm-up ramp, recomputed on every read. Sent back on a write it is accepted and ignored, so the whole document round-trips; it is never stored and never ledgered.

activity_window.description: NOT ACCEPTED. Send its settable subfields instead: the top-level `timezone`, and per row `activity_window_start`, `activity_window_end`, `activity_window_timezone`, `activity_window_applies_to`.

raiseCeiling.summary: Raise one row's ceiling far above the default

tightenOneRow.summary: Enforce on one row, leaving every other field untouched

tenantDefault.summary: Set the workspace-wide posture default for EVERY account in the tenant

limitProfile.summary: Move the account onto the Sales Navigator defaults

activityWindowOn.summary: Switch the activity window on by telling Curviate the account's timezone

activityWindowAll.summary: Hold live READS to the window too, not only writes

clearHalt.summary: Lift the platform pause on one action type now, instead of waiting it out

activityWindowHours.summary: Narrow one row's activity window to office hours

get.summary: List what Curviate refused or warned about

parameters.name: account_id
parameters.description: The account ID (`acc_...`) whose safety events to read.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Pagination cursor from a previous response; decodable, pass it back verbatim.

parameters.name: budget_row
parameters.description: Return only events flagged against this budget row. Omit for every row.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Only events at or after this instant (ISO-8601, e.g. 2026-09-01T00:00:00Z).

parameters.name: until
parameters.description: Only events strictly before this instant (ISO-8601).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many events to return per page, 1 to 100. Defaults to 50.

200.description: What Curviate refused or warned about on this account, newest first. Filter by `budget_row` to ask about one action type, and by `since` / `until` to ask about a period.

id.description: The event's id. Also the value encoded in the next page's cursor.

budget_row.description: The budget row that breached. It is not always a row the call itself spends: an invitation refused because the outstanding backlog is at its ceiling reports `pending_invites`, which is the thing that breached. `*` means the event was not about a row at all: the activity window closing on an action that spends no budget of its own, such as editing a message or a Recruiter admin action. The `budget_row` filter accepts real row names only, so page without it to see those.

reason.description: Which rule flagged it, and each one calls for a different response. `budget_exhausted`: the account reached the ceiling configured for that row, which you can raise on the safety policy. `activity_window`: the account was acting outside its configured activity window, so no ceiling was the constraint. Wait for the window to open, move `activity_window_start` or `activity_window_end`, or check `activity_window_timezone` is the zone you meant. `rate_limited`: the platform itself refused this account on that row recently and Curviate is holding the row until the pause expires. No ceiling you raise lifts it; the one thing that does is `clear_halts` on the safety policy, which lifts it deliberately and records that it was lifted. `halt_cleared` is the odd one out and the only entry that is not a refusal: somebody lifted one of those platform pauses early through `clear_halts` on the safety policy, so the row was open again from that instant. It carries `blocked: false` and its `method` is `update_safety_policy` rather than the operation that breached. Read it beside the `rate_limited` entry it lifts: the pause and its lifting are one thread, and an entry list that showed only the first would report a row as still paused.

blocked.description: Whether the action was stopped. `false` is a warning: the action went through, and this record is the only lasting trace that it crossed a limit. Under the default `warn` posture every event is a warning, which is what makes reading this surface the point of running it. A `halt_cleared` entry is also `false`, for a different reason: it stopped nothing, it lifted a stop.

method.description: The operation the caller was running when it breached.

items.description: Flagged events, newest first. [] when this account has never breached a limit.

cursor.description: Cursor for the next page; null on the terminal page. Pass it back verbatim. Page until cursor is null.

default.summary: A warning that let the action through, two refusals that did not, one per rule, and an operator lifting an earlier platform pause

empty.summary: Nothing has been flagged on this account

400.description: Invalid request: an out-of-range `limit`, an unknown `budget_row`, a malformed `since` / `until`, or a corrupt `cursor`.

value.message: A parameter failed validation.

404.description: No such account for this tenant. An id whose connection was replaced or removed also stops resolving here, and it is already absent from the list, so re-read `GET /v1/accounts` for the current id.

value.message: The referenced resource does not exist for this tenant.

429.description: Rate limited, slow down and retry after the hinted delay.

value.message: The per-account request rate limit was exceeded; retry after the delay in retry_hint. Per-workspace breaches carry RATE_LIMIT_TENANT; ingress-wide breaches (pre-auth, no per-client key) and upstream saturation both carry PLATFORM_RATE_LIMIT. A 429 on a budgeted action can also be BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, which is Curviate's own account-safety ceiling rather than a request-rate limit: it never reached LinkedIn, spent nothing, and carries row, reset_at and hint.

get.description: Returns this account's safety events, newest first: every action Curviate refused, and every action it let through while flagging that a limit had been crossed. Under the default posture nothing is refused, so everything here is a warning and `blocked` is how you tell the two apart. Each event names the budget row that breached, why, the operation that hit it and when. Filter by `budget_row` for one action type and by `since` / `until` for a period, and page until `cursor` is null. This is a read of what already happened, so it never changes a limit or a count: to change what is refused, update the safety policy. The account resource is the other half of the picture, reporting where each row stands right now rather than what has already been flagged. One entry here is not a refusal: `reason: "halt_cleared"` with `blocked: false` records somebody lifting a platform pause early through `clear_halts` on the safety policy, and it sits beside the `rate_limited` entry it lifted so the pause and its end read as one thread.
